encounters.cc: Feeling slightly lightheaded and has a brief moment of blurry vision during physiology experiment

lines: Feeling slightly lightheaded and has a brief moment of blurry vision during physiology experiment
He volunteers for a clinical physiology experiment.
He is hooked up to non-invasive hemodynamic monitoring equipment while resting comfortably on a table in a supine position.
After 10 minutes of rest, he is asked to stand up quickly and remain upright.
Within a few seconds, he reports feeling slightly lightheaded and has a brief moment of blurry vision.
These symptoms resolve spontaneously within 15–20 seconds without any intervention.
He is able to continue standing without support, and subsequent testing shows normalization of perfusion.
The research team observes predictable changes in his cardiovascular parameters as part of the physiologic response to orthostasis.
Active Problem List:
- Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus
He has never had similar symptoms before.
- Craniotomy with evacuation of traumatic epidural hematoma
He does not take any medications.
Home Medications:
- Insulin glargine 24 units subcutaneous at bedtime
- Insulin lispro 1 unit per 10 grams carbohydrates with meals
NKDA
- Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus in father
- Autoimmune thyroid disease in mother
- Hypertension in paternal grandfather
He exercises regularly
He reports no chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath.
His blood pressure decreases mildly upon standing and then quickly returns to baseline.
His heart rate increases moderately but appropriately.
No abnormalities are noted on physical exam or subsequent neurologic assessment.
Cognitive testing reveals intact memory, orientation, and attention.
These changes are transient and reflect normal autonomic reflexes in healthy individuals.
The researchers explain that his symptoms were caused by a brief mismatch in perfusion and autonomic compensation.
The protocol notes state that this is an expected physiologic phenomenon.

lines: Disoriented and vomiting after reported aspirin ingestion

Earlier in the day, the patient had mentioned taking "a bunch of aspirin" after a heated argument with his parents.

lines: Sudden nausea, vomiting, and watery diarrhea started 4 hours ago

The patient is a 29-year-old male with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus who presents to the Emergency Department with acute gastrointestinal symptoms, returning approximately one year after a prior admission for diabetic ketoacidosis.
He reports that the symptoms began suddenly while he was at work and have been persistent throughout the day.
He denies fever, chills, abdominal pain, or blood in the stool.
He has not traveled recently, had no recent sick contacts, and has not taken antibiotics in the past year.
He states that the only unusual thing he ate was leftover fried rice from a takeout container that he reheated in the microwave the night before.

encounters.cc: Three days of profuse watery diarrhea after returning from Mexico

lines: Three days of profuse watery diarrhea after returning from Mexico
This 30-year-old male with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus, previously treated for Bacillus cereus food poisoning in January 2025, presents with profuse watery diarrhea.
He recently returned from a 2-week backpacking trip through rural areas of southern Mexico.
During the trip, he drank untreated water and ate from several street food vendors.
He reports 7–8 loose, brownish-green bowel movements daily, accompanied by mild abdominal cramping, but denies blood in the stool, fever, or vomiting.
His appetite is reduced, and he feels fatigued, but he is still able to stay hydrated with oral fluids.
